item.title: Lisa Stulberg, "How to Win a Culture War" — Thu Oct 29, 7:00 PM — watchung booksellers the kids’ room
item.description:
Watchung Booksellers welcomes author Lisa M. Stulberg for the release of How to Win a Culture War: LGBTQ+ Social Change Through Pop Culture, on Thursday, Oct 29 at 7:00 p.m. In How to Win a Culture War, sociologist Lisa M. Stulberg argues that, despite substantial barriers, past and current creatives and athletes are changing American culture through their contributions to arts, sports, and politics. Tickets are $5 and include a 10% discount on the book purchased at the event. Students may attend free of charge by emailing events@watchungbooksellers.com. item.title: What We Need To Know About Data Centers — Thu Oct 29, 7:00 PM — Verona Park Boathouse
item.description:
Do AI Data Centers pose an existential threat to our environment or can site review and regulation minimize their impact on water and air quality and power consumption? New Jersey Sierra Club Director Anjuli Ramos and Chapter Organizer Maegan Kuhlmann will discuss these issues and what Sierra Club is doing at the state and local level to protect communities from uncontrolled data center development in a Gateway Group membership meeting on Thursday, October 29 at 7 PM at the Verona Park Boathouse. The meeting is open to Sierra Club members and the general public.Pre-registration is requested, but last minute walk-ins are welcome. item.title: Suzanne Vega Live in Concert — Fri Oct 30, 8:00 PM — first congregation church
item.description: Outpost in the Burbs presents Suzanne Vega in concert in Montclair. Ms Vega will perform a career-spanning show including favorites like “Tom’s Diner”, “Luka”, “Marlene On The Wall”, and many more, plus songs from her latest album, Flying with Angels, which was released in May 2025 to critical acclaim. She will be joined on stage by her longtime guitarist, Gerry Leonard (of David Bowie fame), and cellist Stephanie Winters. Widely regarded as one of the foremost songwriters of her generation, Suzanne Vega emerged as a leading figure of the folk revival of the early 1980s. Accompanying herself on acoustic guitar, Vega sang what has been called contemporary folk or neo-folk songs of her own creation in Greenwich Village clubs. Since the release of her self-titled, critically acclaimed 1985 debut album, she has given sold-out concerts in many of the world’s best-known venues. item.title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays) — Sun Nov 8, 9:00 AM
item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).
**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one

item.description:
What does the library mean to you? As we prepare for our upcoming renovation, we want to build a space that truly serves our community—and that starts with listening to you.
Join us for an open feedback session to share whatever is on your mind:
How you use the library today
What you love about our programs, collections, and spaces
Frustrations or obstacles you've run into
What you’d love to see in the renovated space
Whether you have big design ideas or just want to tell us about your favorite books, we're all ears. Your feedback will directly guide the design, programs, and future of our library.

item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Tue Oct 27, 7:00 PM
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Watchung Booksellers Hosts Ann Martin Ridings, "A Woven Woman" — Tue Oct 27, 7:00 PM — watchung booksellers the kids’ room
item.description:
Watchung Booksellers welcomes Ann Martin Ridings, author of the newly released memoir, A Woven Woman, on Tuesday, October 27 at 7:00 p.m. A Woven Woman is a lyrical, hybrid memoir composed in a distinct style— a stream of diary, poem, essay and observation—held together by emotional through-lines rather than chronology. In it, Ann uncovers motherhood, childhood, artistic identity, ancestral traces, and the hidden cartographies of a woman’s life.
